Head 1 · Project start: from text memory to cheap models

sections.title: Summary
blocks: Eykon is a **second brain for a phone**: a persistent, local-first memory. It reads what the user records (video and its sound), keeps the moments worth remembering with their context in SQLite, and later answers questions with proof: the frame, the time, the quote. Nothing leaves the device at runtime.

This head documents how the project got to its current shape. It started as a typed-notes memory on a laptop (Phase 1), was made accurate by a three-stage retrieval pipeline (Phase 1.1), was ported to Android with on-device answers and voice (Phase 2), and was then extended to video by captioning every frame with a vision-language model (Phase 3).

Phase 3 worked but was **too heavy for a phone**: about 13 s per frame on the laptop CPU and 4.68 W average on the Infinix Note 12. On 12 October 2026 the project changed direction: small specialised models describe frames instead (Option A), the VLM is kept only as an optional last resort and a comparison baseline, and the product is built once, on the phone.

blocks.note: **Priority order of what Eykon must do:** (1) find objects: "where are my keys?", "where were they yesterday?"; (2) speech and actions: "what did I say about X?", "what was I doing?"; (3) sounds without words, meetings and lectures (important, later).

sections.title: Approach: how each phase was built

blocks.h3: Phase 1 · Text memory on the laptop

blocks: Goal: prove the core loop. The user types a memory, the app stores it, the user asks a question, the app retrieves the right memory and a local LLM writes a grounded answer.

rows: Fastest way to a usable product screen
512-token context, about 45 MB, strong MTEB accuracy
Simple, no vector database needed at this scale
Exact and fast enough for hundreds of memories
Same model and runtime planned for the phone

blocks: Memories are chunked at 256 tokens with 40 tokens of overlap (ceiling 400), embedded, and stored with a keyword index. Search returns the top 5.

The baseline was weak on abstract questions ("Am I financially comfortable?" against a stored "15,000 rupees… 2,000 left by month end"): semantic Hit@1 was only 20 %. Three steps were added, each measured on its own:

steps: **Query expansion (step 09):** a zero-latency dictionary maps abstract words to concrete ones ("stress" to "exam, deadline, sleep") before embedding. No LLM needed.
**Widen the pool (step 10):** take the top 20 from dense vectors and the top 20 from BM25, fuse them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k = 60), keep 20 candidates.
**Cross-encoder re-ranking (step 11):** ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 (22 M parameters) re-orders the 20 candidates against the original question and returns the top 5.

blocks: All three were switched on by default for the demo (TOP_K 5, POOL_K 20, EXPAND_QUERY on, RERANK on).
Goal: port the validated Phase 1 loop (capture, embed, store, retrieve, generate) to a native, fully offline Android app and add voice as a second way to capture.

steps: Android project in Kotlin + Jetpack Compose; the Phase 1 storage ported to Room (SQLite).
Typed text capture through the same path as the laptop.
Gemma 4 E2B (.litertlm) through the LiteRT-LM Kotlin API for on-device answers; the 2.4 GB model downloads on first launch with a checksum.
On-device embedding and retrieval with ONNX Runtime.
Voice capture: Whisper transcribes on the phone and the text follows the typed-text path.

blocks: Steps 06 (full UI) and 07 (integration test) were dropped as written: the app was repurposed for video and those checks moved into the phone gate (EYKO-34).

blocks.h3: Phase 3 · Video through a vision-language model

blocks: Goal: remember recorded video. Frames are sampled from a video (1 every 5 s by default), a VLM writes a caption for each frame, and the captions go into the same memory and search as text notes.

bullets: Primary VLM: Gemma 4 E2B-it, the same model already used for answers, so no extra RAM for a second model.
Comparison VLMs: Moondream2 (GGUF) and SmolVLM / PaliGemma.
Mobile budget enforced on the laptop: all AI models together within 4 GB of RAM; benchmarks run CPU-only to imitate a phone.
Built: literature review, environment, frame extraction, VLM captioning, video orchestrator, memory integration, Streamlit video UI, benchmark suite, experiments A1 to A3, soak test (steps 01 to 10).

sections.title: Results: where this left the project

bullets: A proven text memory loop with strong retrieval (Hit@5 93.3 %) on the laptop and an Android app that captures text and voice and answers on the device.
A working VLM video path that is too slow and power-hungry for continuous use on a phone, kept in src/vision/ as the Option C reference.
A new plan: the 88-card Synverk board, starting with EYKO-1 (tables) and EYKO-2 (pick a video), built in the Android app with cheap models.

blocks.note: The text notes path (Ask tab: notes in Room, keyword search, Gemma answers) still runs in the app, separate from video. Joining the two is the "Ask & answer" head (EYKO-17 to 24).

sections.title: Limits: how these numbers could mislead

bullets: Phase 1 was scored on 30 questions over a synthetic corpus written for the test; real notes will be messier.
Query expansion uses a hand-written concept map, tuned while looking at the same 30 questions.
Phase 3 experiments A1 to A3 used 3 short clips and 9 questions: smoke tests, not evidence.
The 13 s per frame figure is a laptop CPU number; the phone was only measured for power, not per-frame speed, on this path.
The cross-encoder adds about 1 s per query on the laptop; its cost on a phone has not been measured.
